newsitem.title: JAPAN: All months of Tokyo corn futures fall on USDA data.
newsitem.headline: All months of Tokyo corn futures fall on USDA data.

text.p: All months of Tokyo corn futures fell by early Thursday afternoon, as bearish sentiment spread after the U.S. Department of Agriculture's optimistic grain production forecast overnight, local traders said.
Prices were 380 to 470 yen lower in early afternoon. Benchmark September was down 450 yen at 17,150 yen per tonne.
The USDA overnight said the 1996 U.S. corn crop would total 8.804 billion bushels, above its forecast in August of 8.695 billion.
Traders said selling emerged in the Tokyo corn market from local investors.
CBOT Project A trading also eased as selling orders from Asian traders remained.
The December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.25-1/2 per bushel at 0545 GMT, against $3.26-3/4 at Wednesday's close.
CBOT November soybean futures on the overnight trading system were at $8.01-1/2 at 0545 GMT, against $8.05 at Wednesday's close.
